title: Fish a cable through a conduit with a fish tape
instruction: Pull the orange cable through the grey conduit with the yellow fish tape: hook the cable's eyelet onto the fish-tape hook at the conduit's right-hand end, then pull the tape back out of the left-hand end until the eyelet is at least 5 cm out of the conduit.
context: Electricians (O*NET 47-2111.00, core task: "pull insulated wires or cables through the conduit to complete circuits between boxes") cannot reach inside a raceway, so they fasten the cable to a fish tape already pushed through it and pull the tape back by hand. Here one arm holds the tape steady while the other hooks the cable on; the first arm then pulls the tape back hand over hand.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases on the table (x forward, y left). Matte grey baseboard 14 x 60 x 0.5 cm centred x 36, y 1. On it, fixed: straight light-grey conduit, 30 cm long along y from y -16 (right mouth) to y 14 (left mouth), axis at x 36, square 26 x 26 mm bore, 3 mm walls. Yellow 4.8 mm round fibreglass fish tape, 46 cm, threaded through it: steel hook (20 mm stem, 4 x 4 mm prong 20 mm tall at its tip, pointing up) 6 cm out of the right mouth; black 40 x 14 x 9 mm handle 12 cm out of the left mouth. Orange 6 mm PVC cable, 66 cm, loose and straight on the table from x 84, y -63 to its eyelet, which points towards x 24, y -28: steel lug 28 x 9 x 7 mm plus a square ring (18 mm outside, 12 mm hole, 3 mm bars, lying flat).
scoring: Score 0 if: the eyelet is ever inside the conduit (centre 2 cm or more past the right mouth) while not on the hook (pushed in by hand); or at the end the eyelet is off the hook (prong not through the ring); or the cable does not run from the eyelet back through the bore and out of the right mouth (e.g. carried around the outside). Otherwise, at the end, eyelet on the hook: 1.0 if its centre is at least 5 cm past the left mouth; 0.75 if it is out by less than 5 cm; 0.5 if it is inside the conduit; 0.25 if it is still at the right mouth with no cable inside the conduit.
reset_notes: Unhook the eyelet and pull the cable back out. Push the fish tape back from the left until the hook prong is 6 cm out of the right mouth, standing up. Lay the cable straight on its tape marks (tail at x 84, y -63; ring centre at x 24, y -28), ring flat. The conduit and baseboard are clamped down; a trial in which either moves is void and re-run.
fidelity: Cable and tape are chains of 2 cm rigid segments with bending springs, no twist, no plasticity; the tape is round (as fibreglass fish tapes are). Hook and eyelet are rigid boxes on the end segments; the eyelet is held only by contact with the prong (no latch, no tape wrap). Square, smooth-bore conduit instead of round. On the hook = prong axis crosses the ring plane within 9.5 mm of the ring centre. Real tapes end in an eyelet the wire is tied to; here the tape has a hook instead.
